key: Ask which hormone drives the finding: estradiol with spironolactone grows breasts, shrinks testes and brings clotting and potassium risks, while testosterone deepens the voice, stops menses and raises the hematocrit.
items: Estradiol stimulates ductal and stromal breast growth, and the change is largely permanent.
Spironolactone blocks aldosterone as well as androgen receptors, so serum potassium can rise.
Estradiol suppresses LH, so testosterone falls and testicular volume and erections decrease.
Higher clotting risk with oral estrogen
Oral estrogen passes through the liver first and raises clotting factors, so venous thromboembolism rises.
Lower testosterone and added estradiol reduce sebum and muscle mass over months.
Estradiol reduces sperm production, so sperm cryopreservation is offered before the first dose.
Estrogen raises hepatic triglyceride output and bile cholesterol saturation, which promote gallstones.
Testosterone stimulates erythropoietin, so red cell mass and hematocrit climb and need regular checks.
Androgens thicken the vocal folds, a permanent change that estrogen cannot reverse.
Clitoral tissue carries androgen receptors and grows under testosterone, a change that persists.
Testosterone suppresses the ovarian cycle and thins the endometrium, so bleeding usually stops.
Suppressed ovarian estrogen thins the vaginal epithelium, causing dryness and pain with intercourse.
Androgens stimulate sebaceous glands and shrink scalp follicles in susceptible patients.
Testosterone reduces HDL and can raise triglycerides, so lipids are followed on therapy.
